macro.regime: Hawkish hold meets an oil-shock war (risk-on bounce)
macro.narrative: Re-verified Wed 22 Jul 07:00 SGT (pre-Asia-open) against the Tue 21 Jul US close. The regime call is unchanged — a hawkish hold colliding with an oil-shock war — but risk appetite bounced hard on Tuesday: US stocks snapped a three-day losing streak (S&P +0.89% to 7,509, Nasdaq +1.29% to 25,837) on a memory-chip surge (Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%, AMD +8% on its Microsoft AI deal), silver ripped ~4% to ~$59, gold rose ~1.3-1.75% back above $4,060, and BTC hit a five-week high ~$66.5k. A 10-day ceasefire proposal (Qatar/Egypt/Pakistan) is on the table even as the US ran a 10th night of strikes, Houthis blockaded Saudi and tankers were hit near Hormuz (transits -66%, Brent ~$89-90). The rates channel still caps the metals thesis longer-term — the 28-29 Jul FOMC is ~85%+ hold, markets price ~zero 2026 cuts with residual September-hike risk, and Chair Warsh keeps 'prices are too high'. But the near-term tape improved: breadth firmed (S&P >200-DMA back to ~68.6%, highest since Feb), semis reversed higher, credit spreads stay tight. BofA's Bull & Bear near ~9.6 is still an extreme contrarian-sell, so the bounce is into stretched positioning. Watch: the ceasefire feelers, next week's FOMC, Lynas results today, and Thursday's S-REIT earnings.

drivers.read: 10th night of US strikes but a 10-day ceasefire proposal (Qatar/Egypt/Pakistan) is now on the table; Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi, two tankers were struck near Hormuz and weekly transits fell ~66%. Brent held ~$89-90, WTI low-$80s; oil ~$20 above year-ago keeps the inflation impulse alive and residual September-hike risk on the table — still the dominant swing factor, with the ceasefire the key de-escalation watch.

Headline CPI -0.4% m/m (biggest drop since 2020), +3.5% y/y; core cooled to +2.6% y/y (0.0% m/m) — the feared hot-core did NOT materialize. A genuine disinflation signal, but the subsequent oil spike clouds the read and Warsh cautioned against 'mission accomplished'

Sharp reversal: after SOX -11% on the month and SMH ~20% off its late-June peak, memory led a Tuesday rebound (Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%, AMD +8% on its Microsoft AI deal) as ~88% of the ~66 S&P names reported beat EPS. The bounce repairs last week's washout but is earnings-contingent on this week's megacap AI results; Burry's chip shorts still a structural counter-view.

drivers.factor: Precious metals bounce but stay capped by rates
drivers.read: Silver ripped ~4% Tuesday to ~$59 and gold rose ~1.3-1.75% back above $4,060, joining the risk-on rebound off the $4,000 shelf — the strongest metals up-day in weeks. But both remain in a rates-driven correction (silver still ~50% below its January record) and the driver is risk appetite, not a real-rates thaw; the FOMC next week is the arbiter. Still the book's highest-beta pain point despite the bounce.

HK tech kept rallying: Alibaba (9988) surged on pre-earnings optimism (narrowing losses) and the Apple Intelligence China approval with Alibaba's Qwen as the foundational model; Tencent (0700) and Chinese AI names rode the same enthusiasm plus the national-team put (CSRC support, state-fund buying, LPRs held 3.00%/3.50%). One of the few risk pockets with a visible policy floor — fiscal follow-through at the late-July Politburo is the swing.

drivers.factor: Fed higher-for-longer; July hold near-certain, September-hike tail
drivers.read: Prediction markets put the 28-29 July FOMC at ~85%+ hold and ~76% odds of zero 2026 cuts (only ~20% for even one 25bp cut); residual September-hike risk persists on the oil-inflation impulse. Chair Warsh keeps 'prices are too high'; June SEP pencils PCE ~3.6% for 2026. 10Y ~4.63% (up ~3bp as stocks rallied), no SEP at the July meeting. Cuts remain off the table — the durable headwind for rate-sensitive sleeves.

drivers.factor: Breadth firmed with the Tuesday rebound
drivers.read: Breadth recovered with Tuesday's broad rally: ~68.6% of the S&P is back above its 200-DMA (highest since February) after dipping to ~64% last week, advancers led ~2:1, and net new highs recovered from Monday's negative print. Momentum is still light — the McClellan Summation sits at a divergent lower high — so this is a healthy bounce, not a confirmed fresh thrust; megacap AI earnings this week are the test.

byAssetClass.note: S&P closed +0.89% at 7,509 and Nasdaq +1.29% at 25,837 Tuesday, snapping a three-day losing streak on a memory-led semis rebound (Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%). Breadth firmed (~68.6% above the 200-DMA, highest since Feb) with ~88% of reporters beating EPS, but BofA's Bull & Bear near ~9.6 flags stretched positioning and the Warsh Fed caps multiple expansion. Stay benchmark-weight with a quality tilt; the bounce is real but earnings-contingent into next week's FOMC.

Two-sided but firmer: energy holds a war premium (Brent ~$89-90) on the Hormuz blockade/tanker strikes, and precious metals staged a strong Tuesday bounce (silver +4% to ~$59, gold back above $4,060). Modest OW on the energy/war hedge plus the metals relief, but the metals sleeve still needs the oil-inflation impulse and higher-for-longer rates to fade before it can durably base.

BTC hit a five-week high ~$66.5k Tuesday as risk appetite returned, ETH and SOL firming off recent lows — a clear risk-on turn, though still below the Oct-2025 ATH (~$126k). Regulatory tailwinds build (US CLARITY Act; Japan crypto reclassification). Rate/flow sensitivity stays a headwind under a hawkish Fed; keep sizing small, convexity improves on a Fed pivot or CLARITY passage.

10Y ~4.63% (up ~3bp as equities rallied), 2Y ~4.2x%; the risk-on session pushed yields up modestly. HY OAS historically tight (~262bp). Favor the belly/quality credit for carry; the oil-driven inflation tail and residual September-hike risk argue against maxing duration, but a growth scare or renewed equity selloff would reward it.

Cash yields ~3.6-3.9% at the fed-funds floor with the dollar firm (DXY ~100.5-100.7) on the war bid and higher-for-longer. Positive nominal carry and optionality while an Iran escalation and a September-hike tail stay live — the big cash pile is dry powder for the metals/rare-earth pullbacks. pUp12m reflects near-certain positive cash return offset by two-way USD direction.
